sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: FAME is a **demand-side incentive** scheme designed to bridge the price gap between Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles and Electric Vehicles (EVs).
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The scheme is administered by the **Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI)**, focusing on technology development, demand creation, and pilot projects.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: It operates on the principle of **Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP)** to encourage domestic value addition and reduce import dependency on critical components like cells and motors.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** is the primary economic metric used to justify the subsidy, aiming to make EVs competitive with ICE vehicles over the vehicle's lifecycle.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Pilot phase; focused on technology demonstration and initial demand creation.
Budgetary support for R&D and charging infrastructure.
Prelims: Focus on initial scope and limited coverage.
Scale-up phase; focus on electrification of public transport and shared mobility.
Demand incentives for 2W, 3W, and e-buses; emphasis on localization.

items.definition: Direct subsidy provided to buyers of EVs to reduce the upfront purchase price, thereby stimulating market demand.
A policy tool mandating a gradual increase in the percentage of locally manufactured components in EVs to qualify for subsidies.
The network of AC and DC fast-charging stations supported under FAME to address 'range anxiety'.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Public Transport Electrification**: Deployment of e-buses in major cities under the FAME-II scheme to reduce urban air pollution.
• **Shared Mobility**: Incentivizing e-rickshaws and e-taxis to promote last-mile connectivity and green public transit.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: High cost of Lithium-ion batteries, lack of standardized charging protocols, and inadequate grid infrastructure.
• **Solutions**: Adoption of Battery Swapping Policy, PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) battery storage, and integration with renewable energy grids.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-I-P' (Demand, Infrastructure, PMP).
• **Decoded Meaning**: D (Demand Incentives), I (Infrastructure/Charging), P (Phased Manufacturing/Localization).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses FAME with the PLI scheme for ACC Battery Storage. FAME is for *demand/adoption*, while PLI is for *supply-side manufacturing* of batteries.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Decarbonization of the Transport Sector' and 'Energy Security' when discussing FAME in the context of India's oil import bill.

keyTakeaways: FAME is a demand-side incentive scheme under the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
It emphasizes domestic manufacturing through the Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP).
The scheme is a critical pillar for achieving India's Net Zero 2070 and NDC targets.
